scenes.headline: How TabFM predicts a table without training on it
scenes.sub: In-context learning over a synthetic prior, in three stages.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Mimosa! Tabular data has long meant fitting a fresh boosted tree. Google's TabFM skips the fitting. Here's how.

scenes.text: Your labelled rows are the prompt. TabFM reads them as context and predicts a new row in one forward pass, with no training on your data.
scenes.mark: Your labelled rows are the prompt
scenes.say: Your labelled rows are the prompt. TabFM reads them as context and predicts a new row in one pass, never training on your data.

left.title: Fit a boosted tree
items: Boosting rounds on your table, one after another
left.say: A boosted tree must fit your table first, round after round, before it can predict anything.

right.title: TabFM, in context
items: Labelled rows go in as context
right.say: TabFM has no fit loop. The table goes in as context, and the answer comes out of one pass.

items.say: So where does the skill come from? First, sample a random causal graph.
Let it emit synthetic features and a label.
Train one transformer to solve that little prediction problem, in context.

items.text: Repeat, hundreds of millions of times
items.say: Repeat hundreds of millions of times. It learns the algorithm of prediction, not any one dataset.

steps.say: The table goes in whole, labelled rows plus the test row. Column attention works across each row's features, with numbers embedded as Fourier features.
Each row is then pooled into a single CLS token. One vector per row.
A twenty-four block transformer reads all the row vectors together. This is the stage that learns your dataset, with its weights frozen.
Out comes the test row's label. No gradient step ever touched your data.

scenes.title: TabArena classification Elo
scenes.note: no standalone boosted tree in the chart
scenes.say: On TabArena, TabFM leads. But the tree-side rival is AutoGluon, an AutoML ensemble, so read it as ensemble versus ensemble.

scenes.text: Prediction becomes inference over a prompt. The learning happened ahead of time, on synthetic tables.

recap: Labelled rows are context, not training data
Pretrained on hundreds of millions of synthetic tables
Columns, then rows, then a 24-block in-context stack
scenes.say: To recap: rows as context, a synthetic prior, and three stages ending in one forward pass.
